subject: Draft MAP: volume ladder and acceptance criteria
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@atlaslogistics.com>, Tara Singh <tara@atlaslogistics.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwoodinference.com
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Draft MAP: volume ladder and acceptance criteria

Alex / Tara —

Thanks for taking the time last week. Attached is a first-pass Mutual Action Plan (Atlas_MAP_v3.pdf) that ties the evaluation milestones to commercial triggers so we can align on when discounts and committed pricing kick in. High-level asks: confirm the PoC success criteria and the monthly token ramp that makes sense for your teams.

Summary (proposed):
- PoC / Eval (4 weeks): target 2M tokens total, end-to-end latency target < 350ms p95 for your 80-token prompts.
- Post-eval Month 1 (pilot): 1M TPM
- Month 2: 3M TPM
- Month 3: 8M TPM
- Month 4+: committed cadence ramps to 15M TPM by month 6

Commercial triggers:
- If Month 3 sustained >= 8M TPM for two consecutive weeks, Atlas qualifies for a 10% committed discount applied retroactively to month 3 onward.
- If Atlas signs a 12-month committed contract within 30 days of PoC success, additional 5% rebate on year spend if the 12-month commit is met.

I flagged the places where we need your confirmation (acceptance criteria, who owns dataset prep, and whether the 8M TPM target is realistic given your integration timeline).

Next steps: can you confirm by EOD Wednesday whether the PoC criteria and Month1/Month2 targets look feasible? If we get alignment, I’ll push a commercial summary to procurement and draft the HubSpot deal with milestones.

Attachments: Atlas_MAP_v3.pdf (MAP + milestones)

Thanks —
Soojin Lee
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0192
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@atlaslogistics.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@atlaslogistics.com
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Draft MAP: volume ladder and acceptance criteria

Soojin —

Thanks for the draft. A few quick clarifications from the engineering side: 
1) The 80-token prompt is only representative; our average prompt is ~220 tokens and our seq len distribution skews up during certain jobs. Will the 350ms p95 target hold at 220 tokens?
2) For the PoC baseline, do you expect the 2M tokens to be single-threaded user flows or parallelized batch runs? Our initial integration will likely spike concurrency.

Procurement looped in; they want to see the commercial ladder before they prepare an intake form.

—Alex
Alex Chen
Head of ML Platforms | Atlas Logistics
alex.chen@atlaslogistics.com
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@atlaslogistics.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Draft MAP: volume ladder and acceptance criteria

Alex —

Quick technical note: the 350ms p95 at 80 tokens was conservative for client demos. At 220 tokens we should expect ~480ms p95 on the exact same hardware profile; with our recommended quantized runtime and the KV cache we can get that down toward ~420ms p95 for typical seq lengths. The attached rinf_perf_guide.pdf has a short table mapping seq length -> expected p95 across our standard instance types.

About the PoC load profile: we recommend a hybrid of parallelized requests (to validate concurrency) and steady-state sustained throughput. For the 2M token PoC we suggest a 48-hour soak with a peak concurrency window to validate autoscaling behavior.

Suggested refined MAP ramp (operationally realistic):
- PoC success: 2M tokens total with 48h soak and 1-week acceptance window
- Pilot (Month 1): 1.2M TPM
- Month 2: 4M TPM
- Month 3: 9M TPM (sustained 2-week window to trigger discount)
- Month 4-6: linear ramp to 18M TPM by month 6

I can run an internal perf-run against a sanitized sample of your traffic (need a short SSH jumpbox + sample payloads). That should give us confidence the targets are achievable before procurement signs.

Attachment: rinf_perf_guide.pdf

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwoodinference.com
From: Tara Singh <tara@atlaslogistics.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com>, Alex Chen <alex.chen@atlaslogistics.com>
Cc: procurement@atlaslogistics.com
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 14:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Draft MAP: volume ladder and acceptance criteria

Soojin / Alex —

Procurement here. Thank you — this is helpful. A few commercial items we need answered before opening a PO: 
- Price per million tokens at each tier (pilot / Tier1 / Tier2 / committed) and the exact mechanics for the retroactive discount.
- Whether onboarding credits or trial credits are available to offset the PoC usage.
- We prefer a single 12-month committed PO with quarterly checkpoints rather than rolling month-to-month. Will Redwood accept this structure?

Attached is our procurement intake form with fields we’ll populate once we have the pricing ladder.

Attachment: procurement_intake_form.docx

Thanks,
Tara Singh
Procurement Manager | Atlas Logistics
procurement@atlaslogistics.com
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tara Singh <tara@atlaslogistics.com>, Alex Chen <alex.chen@atlaslogistics.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwoodinference.com, marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Draft MAP: volume ladder and acceptance criteria

Tara —

Appreciate the clarity. Below is our commercial proposal tied to the MAP milestones. This is intentionally prescriptive so procurement can populate the intake form.

Pricing (USD, per million tokens) — list price then committed tiers:
- Pilot (up to 1.2M TPM): $5,200 per million tokens
- Tier 1 (1.2M - 4M TPM): $4,400 per million tokens
- Tier 2 (4M - 9M TPM): $3,800 per million tokens
- Committed (>=9M TPM sustained): $3,200 per million tokens with a 10% retroactive credit if Month 3 sustained >= 9M TPM for two consecutive weeks.

12-month committed option: sign a 12-month commit to the month-6 target (18M TPM run-rate) and we’ll offer an additional 5% annual rebate if the 12-month commitment is met across the year.

Onboarding credits: we can provide a one-time $25k credit to offset PoC usage for Atlas (applied to hosted usage on first invoice).

Mechanics for retroactive discount: if the PoC -> Month 3 milestone is met (9M TPM sustained as above), we will apply a credit equal to 10% of charges from month 3 through month 6 back to the date the milestone was achieved.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Procurement confirms preferred billing model (monthly invoice vs quarterly invoice) and issues the intake form.
2) Atlas sign the commercial summary (I’ll create a short SOW + redline template).
3) We run Ben’s perf validation with a sanitized sample to validate seq length/latency assumptions.

Draft deal created in HubSpot: ATL-2026-1121. I’ll also circulate a DocuSign for signature once procurement confirms billing cadence.

—
Soojin
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 08:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Draft MAP: volume ladder and acceptance criteria

Team —

This looks like a strong path to a healthy enterprise ARR. Approve a $25k onboarding credit (per Soojin’s note) and prioritize the perf validation run — if Ben’s results show we can reliably hit the month-3 target, escalate to legal to accelerate the SOW. If procurement stalls on billing cadence, I’m happy to jump on a call with Tara.

Vivek Kulkarni
